D1.reason_for_score: Score 1 (generic or analogical recognition only): No Curtin policy explicitly addresses an autonomous AI agent representing a student in feedback, extension, or appeal discussions using delegated SSO/email credentials. General rules apply by analogy: N001 covers student use of AI in University activities and requires human oversight; N002 and N141 govern student representation/support persons in assessment and misconduct discussions; N149 governs third-party information requests; N005 governs authorised ICT asset use.
D1.negative_search_or_access_note: No Curtin document addresses 'AI agent', 'delegated access' in an identity platform, or autonomous AI representation of students. Supporting procedure 'Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Appropriate Use Procedures' referenced in N005 (p.218 L010-L011) is not in the corpus.

D2.reason_for_score: Score 2 (named role, applicable criteria and decision process, with authority link to AI representation not explicit): Named roles hold decision authority for extensions (Unit Coordinator, Academic Registrar, Head of School/PVC on appeal in N002 PC7), assessment appeals (Head of School/PVC, SPAC, Academic Registrar in N002 PC24-PC25), advocacy permission (SCAP Chair/Appeal Officer in N141; staff in N002), and third-party disclosure verification (receiving staff and Information Disclosure Compliance Officer in N149), with general internal and external Ombudsman review routes (N002, N004, N144). However, no role has explicit authority or criteria to recognise an autonomous AI agent acting via delegated SSO credentials.

D3.reason_for_score: Score 2 (compatible rules, without explicit coordination): N001 (human oversight, privacy/security compliance), N002 (feedback restricted to student/authorised recipients; support person not an advocate unless invited), N141 (support person limits), N149 (identity and authority verification for third parties), and N005 (ICT assets for authorised purposes only) are mutually compatible, but they are not explicitly coordinated for AI agents communicating through a student's own SSO/email credentials.
D3.negative_search_or_access_note: N005 (Sept 2026) superseded N153 (Aug 2022) and removed the explicit password non-disclosure clause (former N153 s.3.3.1) from the policy text, referencing 'Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Appropriate Use Procedures' (not in corpus).

D4.reason_for_score: Score 2 (usable sequence, with a relevant detail unclear): Documented workflows with steps, forms, and timelines exist for assessment extensions (N002 PC7), assessment appeals (N002 PC24), complaints (N004), and third-party information disclosure using the Disclosure of Information and Proxy Authorisation Form or Communication Authorisation (N149). However, procedural steps are unclear for verifying whether an email/SSO communication is from the student or an autonomous AI agent.
D4.negative_search_or_access_note: The 'Disclosure of Information and Proxy Authorisation Form', 'Communication Authorisation', and 'ICT Appropriate Use Procedures' referenced in N149 and N005 are not included in the corpus.

D5.reason_for_score: Score 2 (substantive protection, but a material gap remains): Substantive safeguards protect confidentiality (N149 identity/authority verification and proxy authorisation; N002 feedback security; N017 consent-gated disclosure; N148/N213 breach reporting), representation boundaries (N002/N141 limits on support persons acting as advocates), and procedural fairness/appeal rights (internal review plus WA Ombudsman and National Student Ombudsman). A material gap remains because these controls rely on staff recognising a third-party requestor and cannot verify authority when an AI agent communicates through the student's own authenticated email/SSO credentials.
D5.negative_search_or_access_note: Operational credential-sharing rules in 'ICT Appropriate Use Procedures' (referenced by N005) are absent from the corpus.

D6.reason_for_score: Score 3 (periodic and event-triggered review, ownership, and monitoring-to-revision route): N001 establishes an annual review cycle (and earlier review for significant legislative changes) to respond to evolving AI technology, with named Policy Compliance Officer, Policy Manager, and Approval Authority. N014 sets default 3- and 5-year review cycles plus event-triggered amendments, while N152 mandates continuous disclosure, Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee monitoring, and corrective action.

case_summary.case_note: Curtin's operative policies require human oversight for AI (N001), restrict assessment feedback to the student or authorised persons (N002 PC2), bar support persons from acting as advocates without permission (N002 PC24; N141), and require staff to verify identity and obtain written proxy/communication authorisation before disclosing personal information to third parties (N149, N017). Independent review and external Ombudsman routes apply (N002, N004, N144). However, a critical gap remains against the S6 criterion (verifiable authority before binding academic representation and before disclosure of confidential student information): when an AI agent communicates autonomously using the student's own email/SSO credentials without a human present, staff cannot independently confirm authorisation, and the ICT Appropriate Use Procedures referenced by N005 (which superseded N153) are missing from the corpus.
